ticket.title: nPVR playback remains available after subscription cancellation
ticket.description: SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURE. Environment: isolated demo environment. Register a test user, create a household, add a device, grant an nPVR subscription, log in on the device, record a live test program, finish the recording, force-cancel the subscription, and request GPC for the recording. Actual: the test recording is playable. Expected: the response contains ServiceNotAllowed. Revocation timing, GPC contract and active-playback policy are not supplied.
warnings: Synthetic illustrative report. No private Jira ticket was fetched or analyzed.

triage.summary: The reported playback path appears to allow access after the required subscription is cancelled.
triage.severityReason: Potential authorization bypass on a core playback path. Actual entitlement policy and revocation timing must be confirmed before final classification.
triage.priorityReason: Provisional P1 because the scenario concerns access control. Production exposure, impact and release timing are unknown.
triage.categoryReason: The stated expected behavior denies playback access with ServiceNotAllowed, while the observed flow allows it.
evidence: force-cancel the subscription, and request GPC for the recording
Actual: the test recording is playable.
missingInformation: Cancellation acknowledgement and effective revocation timestamp
Policy for recordings created before cancellation and already-active playback
Whether this affects other devices or households

rca.conclusion: The playback authorization path may use stale or insufficient entitlement information. The report alone cannot establish a root cause.

hypotheses.cause: Playback authorization does not revalidate the current nPVR entitlement.
hypotheses.evidence: The fixture reports successful playback after force cancellation. No authorization trace is supplied.
hypotheses.killTest: Inspect the GPC authorization decision using the captured correlation ID. If it checks the correct effective entitlement and denies access, investigate downstream enforcement instead.

hypotheses.cause: A warm entitlement cache still permits playback after cancellation.
hypotheses.evidence: The same logged-in device is used before and after cancellation; this is compatible with stale state but does not prove it.
hypotheses.killTest: Compare fresh and existing sessions after confirmed revocation under the documented propagation policy. If both evaluate current cancelled entitlement, the stale-cache explanation is weakened.

hypotheses.cause: A previously issued playback grant remains valid under an unclear revocation policy.
hypotheses.evidence: A recording existed before cancellation, but grant issuance and reuse are unknown.
hypotheses.killTest: Compare a new GPC grant request with reuse of a pre-cancellation grant. If no prior grant is reused, reject this explanation for the reproduction.

investigationSteps: Capture cancellation acknowledgement, effective entitlement state and GPC timestamps for the synthetic user/household/device.
Trace the GPC authorization decision and identify its entitlement source, cache age and token issuance time.
Compare a fresh session and existing session after the documented revocation boundary.
Confirm policy for existing recordings and active streams with the product owner before interpreting token behavior.
blastRadius: Other devices sharing the same household entitlement
Playback flows sharing the same authorization service or cache
limitations: No implementation, entitlement trace or GPC contract was supplied.
Confidence values are subjective estimates, not measured probabilities.
No production scope, monetary loss or definitive root cause has been established.

strategy.missingTest: A subscription-revocation-to-playback authorization check would cover the reported flow. Existing suite coverage is unknown.
strategy.verification: Repeat the fixture through force cancellation. Once the documented revocation condition is met, request GPC and assert the exact ServiceNotAllowed response error and denial of new playback access.

tests.title: Reject new playback access after force cancellation
steps: Create a user, household and device and grant the nPVR subscription.
Log in, record a live test program and stop or finish recording.
Force-cancel the subscription and verify cancellation acknowledgement and effective entitlement state.
When the documented revocation condition is met, request GPC for the recording.
tests.expected: The response contains exactly ServiceNotAllowed and no usable new playback access is granted.
tests.rationale: Checks the authorization boundary directly. Obtain the actual GPC contract before implementing assertions.

tests.title: Allow playback for a currently entitled user
steps: Create the same recording fixture while keeping the subscription active.
Request GPC with the entitled device session.
tests.expected: Playback authorization succeeds according to the documented contract.
tests.rationale: Positive control prevents an overly broad deny-all fix.

tests.title: Evaluate fresh and existing sessions after revocation
steps: Create the recording and retain the existing device session.
Cancel the subscription and wait for the documented effective revocation condition.
Compare GPC decisions in the existing session and a fresh session.
tests.expected: Both sessions deny new playback access with ServiceNotAllowed once the policy applies.
tests.rationale: Targets stale device or session entitlement state.

tests.title: Check the documented revocation boundary
steps: Obtain the documented revocation/propagation policy and a controllable clock or polling contract.
Request GPC immediately before, at and after the defined effective boundary.
tests.expected: Authorization follows the documented policy; at and after effective revocation, new access is denied. No numeric TTL is assumed.
tests.rationale: Tests time and cache boundaries without inventing requirements.

tests.title: Prevent cross-household entitlement reuse
steps: Use two isolated households with one active and one cancelled nPVR subscription.
Request the cancelled household's recording using each authorized test identity according to the ownership contract.
tests.expected: The cancelled household cannot inherit another household's entitlement; ownership and authorization checks remain enforced.
tests.rationale: Checks the scope of entitlement decisions.

tests.title: Restore access only after valid re-subscription
steps: Verify the cancelled state denies new playback.
Re-subscribe the synthetic household and wait for documented entitlement activation.
tests.expected: Access is restored only when activation and recording-retention policy allow it.
tests.rationale: Covers the complete user-visible state transition.

manualChecks: Confirm the intended policy for pre-existing recordings, token reuse and already-active streams.
Review the user-facing message when ServiceNotAllowed is returned.
exitCriteria: Fresh/warm session, revocation boundary and scope regressions pass.
The product owner confirms the revocation and existing-recording policy.
